# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 80 A ESC: Systems Architecture Model

## 0. Scope and Assumptions

I don't have the Job #38 design files, BOM, or stack-up. Everything below is a **parametric reference model** with stated default values. Replace the values marked ⚙ with your datasheet numbers and the equations still hold.

**Architecture clarification.** In a 4-in-1 ESC, the 48 kHz phase PWM is generated by the **ESC-side MCUs** (AM32 or BLHeli_32 on AT32/STM32G0-class parts), not by the H743. The H743 runs ArduPilot and drives four bidirectional DShot600 lines to those MCUs. The model is split accordingly:

| Domain | Owner | Sections |
|---|---|---|
| Power stage (conduction, switching, thermal) | ESC MCU + gate drivers + 24 MOSFETs | 1–3 |
| Motor command and eRPM telemetry | STM32H743 timers + DMA (ArduPilot) | 4 |
| Interconnect | Netlists | 5 |

**Default operating point:**

| Symbol | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| V_bus | 25.2 V | 6S full charge |
| I_burst | 80 A per motor channel | Burst, not continuous |
| f_sw | 48 kHz | |
| R_DS(on),25 | 0.70 mΩ ⚙ | 40 V class, 3.3×3.3 or 5×6 PQFN |
| α (R_DS tempco) | ≈0.0045 /K ⚙ | |
| t_r, t_f | 15 ns each ⚙ | At ~2 A gate drive, Q_gd ≈ 10 nC |
| Q_rr | 50 nC ⚙ | |
| Q_oss | 60 nC ⚙ | |
| Q_g | 50 nC ⚙ | At V_GS = 10–12 V |
| t_dead | 100 ns | |
| V_SD (body diode) | 0.8 V | |
| Board | 8-layer, 2 oz inner copper, ~30×30 mm ESC | |

---

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Commutation topology
Trapezoidal six-step drive with synchronous complementary PWM works as follows. In each 60° sector, one phase leg PWMs and one low-side is held on.

- The PWM leg's high-side conducts for duty D.
- The PWM leg's low-side conducts for (1 − D) as a synchronous rectifier.
- The static low-side conducts 100% of the time.

### 1.2 RMS current with ripple
$$
I_{rms}^2 = I^2 + \frac{\Delta I_{pp}^2}{12}, \qquad
\Delta I_{pp} = \frac{(V_{bus} - V_{bemf})\,D}{2L_{ph}\,f_{sw}}
$$

For a typical 5–7" motor, L_ph ≈ 15–30 µH, so ΔI_pp ≈ 2–6 A. The ripple term adds less than 0.1% at 80 A and is neglected below. Keep it for low-inductance motors.

### 1.3 Temperature-dependent resistance
$$
R_{DS}(T_j) = R_{DS,25}\,[1 + \alpha(T_j - 25)]
$$

At T_j = 125 °C: R_DS = 0.70 × 1.45 ≈ **1.02 mΩ**.

### 1.4 Per-channel conduction loss
$$
P_{cond} = I^2 R_{DS}\,[D + (1-D)] + I^2 R_{DS} = 2\,I^2 R_{DS}(T_j)
$$

The result is independent of D, because synchronous rectification makes the PWM leg always conduct through one FET.

$$
P_{cond} = 2 \times 80^2 \times 1.02\times10^{-3} = \mathbf{13.1\ W/channel}\ (\text{hot}),\quad 9.0\ \text{W (cold)}
$$

### 1.5 Copper loss
Phase pad to FET to bus spreading, roughly 0.15 mΩ per current path ⚙:
$$
P_{Cu} \approx 2\,I^2 R_{trace} = 2 \times 6400 \times 0.15\text{ mΩ} \approx 1.9\ \text{W/channel}
$$

The supply side is shared by four channels. With 320 A worst case through the battery pad and 0.1 mΩ, that adds about 10 W board-wide. This is why burst ratings collapse on nano boards. Use fully parallel inner planes and stitching-via fields (≥ 1 A per 0.3 mm via, conservative).

---

## 2. Switching Loss Model (48 kHz)

Only the PWM leg switches. Hard switching happens on the high-side; the low-side commutates through its body diode during dead time.

### 2.1 V–I overlap
$$
P_{VI} = \tfrac{1}{2} V_{bus} I (t_r + t_f) f_{sw} = 0.5 \times 25.2 \times 80 \times 30\text{ns} \times 48\text{k} = \mathbf{1.45\ W}
$$

Rise and fall times from the gate charge:
$$
t_{r,f} \approx \frac{Q_{gd}}{I_g}, \quad I_g \approx \frac{V_{drv} - V_{plateau}}{R_g + R_{g,int}}
$$

### 2.2 Reverse recovery of the low-side body diode
$$
P_{rr} = Q_{rr} V_{bus} f_{sw} = 50\text{n} \times 25.2 \times 48\text{k} = 0.06\ \text{W}
$$

### 2.3 Output capacitance
$$
P_{oss} = Q_{oss} V_{bus} f_{sw} \approx 60\text{n} \times 25.2 \times 48\text{k} \approx 0.07\ \text{W}
$$

This is a conservative upper bound; split ½ per edge if Q_oss is energy-equivalent.

### 2.4 Dead-time body-diode conduction
$$
P_{dt} = V_{SD}\, I\, (2 t_{dead}) f_{sw} = 0.8 \times 80 \times 200\text{ns} \times 48\text{k} = \mathbf{0.61\ W}
$$

### 2.5 Gate drive
This loss is dissipated mostly in the driver and gate resistors:
$$
P_{g} = 2\,Q_g V_{drv} f_{sw} = 2 \times 50\text{n} \times 12 \times 48\text{k} = 0.06\ \text{W}
$$

P_{sw
